question: What does the SDF Bug Bounty pay for a Stellar protocol vulnerability versus a Soroban smart-contract exploit?

golden.answer: Since 2026-05-07 SDF runs one HackerOne bug bounty for new general reports; the Stellar Immunefi program is deprecated for new submissions. Standard maxima run from 25,000 points (critical) to 500 (note); one point is $1, paid in XLM. A carveout pays critical stellar-core, protocol and Soroban host bugs up to 250,000 points. Third-party Soroban apps are outside SDF's program.
keyFacts: New general SDF reports go to the consolidated HackerOne program; Immunefi is deprecated.
Standard maxima run 25,000 (critical) to 500 (note) points; 1 point is $1, paid in XLM.
A 250,000-point carveout covers stellar-core, protocol and Soroban host code.
Exploits in third-party Soroban apps are outside SDF's bug bounty.
avoid: Do NOT present the old $250K protocol and $50K Soroban-app split as the current reward scale.
golden.notes: stellar.org/grants-and-funding still carries the older $250,000 XLM and $50,000 USD wording (observed 2026-11-14); an attributed quote of it is not a wrong claim but is not the current HackerOne scale. The Audit Bank is not a vulnerability bounty. OpenZeppelin's Stellar Contracts Immunefi bounty is a separate program; naming it is correct but not required.

GT-40 blind reversed the primary top-line after following the cited controlling policy. Policy and intake are volatile; accept dated, scope-aware figures only.
Scout research has surfaced the 2026-05-07 SDF security-program migration to the consolidated HackerOne program since 2026-07-15 (sls-020, resolved; re-checked live 2026-11-02, when the security-program record ranked first). An answer that labels the pre-fix roster as historical is correct; an answer that presents a security-program roster without the HackerOne migration as current is wrong.
